column2: Gary and Astor came from two nations locked in the same race, each determined to be first to leave a footprint upon the moon. Gary's nation moved swiftly, and theirs were the first hands to touch the void of space. But it was Astor whose spirit carried him further still. For when the dust had settled and the sky had been reached, it was his foot, not Gary's, that first pressed into the lunar soil. History remembers the swift. Legend remembers Astor: the only Moon Walker.

Once the prestormic men had mastered the language of numbers, they began to build machines to carry the weight of their reasoning (engines meant to quicken their pursuit of mathematics and logic, a pursuit that soon reached into every field of knowledge). So precise and so swift these inventions became at processing thought itself, that in time, their makers gave rise to minds of silice: creations able to rival the very men who built them.
